subject: Copywriting
title: A/B Testing Headlines at Scale
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: A/B Testing Headlines at Scale.

hook.text: The Huffington Post tested 25 headlines per article. The winner got published. Gut instinct was replaced by data.

buildup.text: A/B testing showed that tiny changes matter. 'How to' vs 'Why you should'—one word shifts clicks by 20-40%.

discovery.text: Upworthy's writers wrote 25 options per post. By headline #20, they found angles they'd never have guessed.

twist.text: Testing optimized for clicks, not quality. The 'best' headline was often the most manipulative, not the truest.

climax.text: Modern publishers balance testing with editorial judgment. Data picks winners; humans set the ethical bounds.

punchline.text: 25 headlines per article. Let data pick the winner.

quiz.question: How many headline options did Upworthy writers create per post?
